title: Run a simulated incident with the tool and make it operable by someone else
problem: A tool that has only been run by its author on known data has never been used for its purpose. Under pressure, the on-call engineer needs to trust the tool's own view of its input, act on its alerts, and leave a record someone else can follow.
context: Final task of the pack. The learner generates a synthetic incident, uses the tool to detect and reason about it, and records the exercise. The service and the incident are simulated and must be described as such.
impact: This is the difference between an alerting script and something a team would put in front of an on-call rotation.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The tool reports on itself in machine-readable form: lines read, rejected by reason, duplicates, covered time range and processing duration. The design names the operational question each field answers.
A timestamped incident record for the simulated incident covers detection (which alert, when), diagnosis, the mitigation decision and how the remaining budget justified it, and follow-up actions.
A runbook entry for each alert says what it means, what to check first, and when not to trust the tool, for example a high rejection count.
A person with only the README goes from clone to a report on the bundled synthetic logs in under a minute.
Someone other than the learner reads a report and the runbook, decides whether to page, and justifies the decision. The result is recorded, including where they hesitated.
Automated tests cover the self-telemetry fields and still cover the earlier scenarios, and pass at the submitted revision.
The learner explains one decision in the incident record they would make differently, and the first thing that breaks when log volume grows a hundredfold.

constraints: Standard library plus a test runner only.
The incident is simulated from synthetic logs. Describing it as a real outage is fabricated evidence.
AC-outside-check requires a real person. A simulated or model-performed walkthrough does not satisfy it, and recording one as satisfied is fabricated evidence.
Do not push to a remote, publish a package or deploy anything as part of this task.

scope.description: Operability of the whole tool and one simulated incident exercise.

investigation_areas: What the on-call engineer must know about the tool's input before trusting its verdict
Which timestamps an incident record needs to reconstruct the decision later
Where a first-time reader of the runbook hesitates, which is discovered by watching one
testing_expectations: Run the project's own test suite. State the exact command in the design.
Perform the quickstart on a clean clone before claiming AC-quickstart.
documentation_requirements: README quickstart, objective file format, runbook and the incident record.
Record the outside check result verbatim, including where the person hesitated.
